name: zucca
description: Regulatory research with cited answers from 21 CFR: search, browse and read U.S. food and dietary supplement regulations, with every passage linked to the official eCFR text.

interface.longDescription:
Zucca is a regulatory research tool. It gives ChatGPT cited answers from Title 21 of the Code of Federal Regulations (21 CFR), the U.S. rules for food labeling, nutrient and health claims, and dietary supplements. No sign-up or API key is needed.

Ask what the regulations require, permit or define, and ChatGPT can search the text, read whole sections in order, and quote the exact rule. Every passage comes back with its section citation and a link to the official text on eCFR, so you can check the answer yourself.

Five read-only tools:
- Search: finds the passages that best answer a question, matching both its words and its meaning.
- Browse: lists the parts held, or every section in a part, with headings.
- Read a section: returns a whole section, or one paragraph of it, in document order.
- Read a passage: returns one passage by the exact id another tool gave.
- Find exact text: finds passages containing an exact phrase.

Coverage: 21 CFR chapter I, subchapters A (General) and B (Food for Human Consumption, including part 190, Dietary Supplements), and chapter II parts 1300 (Definitions) and 1308 (Schedules of controlled substances). Part 1300 says a botanical dietary ingredient that is not anabolic or androgenic is not an anabolic steroid, and part 1308 holds the hemp exclusions. Every response names the parts and edition it covers.

Useful for regulatory, quality and product teams checking labeling rules, nutrient content and health claims, serving sizes and definitions, and whether a hemp or cannabinoid ingredient, or a supplement with a steroid-like ingredient, is excluded from the controlled substance schedules.

Zucca returns regulation text, not legal advice. Always confirm against the official eCFR before relying on it.
defaultPrompt: What does 21 CFR require for declaring added sugars on the Nutrition Facts label?
What is the reference amount customarily consumed for breakfast cereals?
List every section in 21 CFR part 101 that covers health claims.

positive.description: Answer a labeling question with citations
positive.prompt: What does 21 CFR require for declaring added sugars on the Nutrition Facts label? Cite the paragraphs.
positive.expected_behavior: Quotes 21 CFR 101.9(c)(6)(iii): grams of added sugars per serving, indented under Total Sugars as "Includes X g Added Sugars", not required under 1 g when no sugar claims are made, with eCFR links.

positive.prompt: What is the reference amount customarily consumed for breakfast cereals? Give the citation.
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the values from the 21 CFR 101.12(b) table: ready-to-eat cereals 15 g, 40 g or 60 g depending on weight per cup, hot cereal 1 cup prepared or 40 g plain dry, with the citation.

positive.prompt: List every section in 21 CFR part 101 that covers health claims.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists 101.14 and 101.70 through 101.83 with their headings, taken from the part's table of contents rather than a search sample.

positive.prompt: Does 21 CFR use the exact phrase "good source"? Show me where.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows passages containing the phrase, including 21 CFR 101.54 and 101.13(i)(2), each with its citation and eCFR link.

positive.prompt: What must a food meet to be labeled "healthy"? Quote the rule and link to it.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads 21 CFR 101.65(d) and quotes the "healthy" criteria in (d)(3), with eCFR links.

negative.description: Unrelated request. The plugin should not be called because the question has nothing to do with regulations.
negative.prompt: What's the weather in Seattle tomorrow?

negative.description: Personal medical advice. The plugin should not be called, or ChatGPT should say the tools hold regulation text, not medical advice.
negative.prompt: How much vitamin D should I take for my bone pain?

negative.description: Regulation outside coverage. The plugin should not be called, or the tools report that 40 CFR is not held and ChatGPT says so instead of guessing.
negative.prompt: What does 40 CFR say about vehicle emissions?

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Five read-only tools that search, browse and read 21 CFR chapter I subchapters A and B (including part 190, Dietary Supplements) and chapter II parts 1300 and 1308, with citations and eCFR links.
